newsitem.title: USA: IDB approves loans to aid Guatemala peace process.
newsitem.headline: IDB approves loans to aid Guatemala peace process.

text.p: The Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) on Wednesday said its board of directors had approved an $84.8 million loan package for Guatemala, including funds to support its fledgling peace process.
Guatemala's government and guerrilla groups are due to sign a peace accord on Dec. 29 to end a 36-year-long civil war in which about 140,000 people were killed.
"Two loans totalling $50 million are designed to help rebuild physical, social and human capital in areas that were damaged by the armed conflict," the bank said in a statement.

Half of those funds, which were loaned on concessional terms, will be earmarked for health and education projects. One quarter will be devoted to programs to boost production and the remaining money will be reserved for other community projects, it added.
One of the unusual characteristics of the loans is that representatives from the war-ravaged communities will be able to choose which projects will be financed.
The IDB package also included a $34.8 million loan for a program to improve garbage collection and sanitation in Guatemala City, where two landfills and a composting plant will be built.
